note: Not an outline. Concepts, what each depends on, and where the subject naturally breaks.

concepts.practiceOpening: Set a clip's duration, resolution and aspect in the tool, then write the prompt without mentioning them
Cut a story idea down to the one sentence a stranger could repeat
Choose or make the still the clip will start from before writing anything
concepts.visualCandidate: The same beat generated with and without a chosen start frame

concepts.practiceOpening: Name the framing of a planned shot: wide, medium, or close, and what that choice says
concepts.visualCandidate: One subject framed three ways, side by side

concepts.practiceOpening: Decide static or moving, and if moving, what the move tells the viewer
Write one action as beats with timing that fits the duration
Look up what your generator actually supports today: first frame, keyframes, references, extension
concepts.visualCandidate: A dated capability table across generators

concepts.practiceOpening: Name the aesthetic in the first line of every prompt, verbatim
Build one character reference and reuse it across three generations
concepts.visualCandidate: The same reference image producing the same face in three clips

concepts.practiceOpening: Rerun one prompt with and without a fixed seed where supported and compare honestly
Write the light (time of day, direction, palette) once and paste it into every clip's prompt
concepts.visualCandidate: Two clips of one room, relit by the model versus held by the prompt

concepts.practiceOpening: Feed the last frame of clip one as the start frame of clip two
concepts.visualCandidate: Two clips sharing one frame at the seam, marked

concepts.practiceOpening: Deliberately chain two dissimilar frames and watch the model cut instead of transition
concepts.visualCandidate: A failed chain: the lens switch mid-clip

concepts.practiceOpening: Split one complex action into two planned clips instead of one long ask
Place the seam mid-gesture so the motion carries the eye across it
Mark the action line on your own scene and keep every planned shot on one side of it
concepts.visualCandidate: Overhead diagram of a scene with the axis drawn and legal camera positions marked

concepts.practiceOpening: Plan wide first, then mediums and close-ups that agree with the established room
Write a three-shot list (framing, beat, camera, duration, references) before generating anything
concepts.visualCandidate: The shot list itself as a filled planning table

boundaries.why: Everything starts with one honest clip: the container, the single beat, the anchor frame, the framing, the camera. Nothing downstream survives a mushy shot.
Keeping character, style and light stable across generations is its own discipline with its own tools (references, verbatim prose, honest seeds).
Joining clips: frame chaining, its failure mode, the stitch decision, the axis. Assumes the shot and continuity work.
The written shot list that turns a story into a sequence. Last because it uses everything before it.
